newsitem.title: USA: Aegon deal ups worries on Providian credit quality.
newsitem.headline: Aegon deal ups worries on Providian credit quality.

text.p: Wall Street arbitrageurs cheered Aegon NV's $3.5 billion acquisition of Providian Corp's insurance business, but fretted over the credit quality at Providian Bancorp, to be spun off to shareholders before the Aegon deal.

"I think the merger is simple process to get done and its a real plus for Aegon. But the question is about Providian Bank. A lot of their business is giving credit to people who can't get it elsewhere, those who pay the 18 percent (interest rate) and Providian's delinquent account charge-offs have been increasing dramatically," an arbitrageur said.

Early Monday, Providian said its board unanimously approved a merger of its insurance operations with Aegon via a a tax-free exchange of stock valued at $2.62 billion and assumption of about $780 million in debt and $100 million in preferred stock.

As for the spin-off Providian Corp holders will receive one Providian Bancorp share per Providian share and Aegon common shares with a value of $28 per Providian share, subject to a share-price collar.

When Providian announced third quarter results on October 29, its stated "the net credit loss rate for managed unsecured receivables was 5.53 percent at September 30, 1996, up from third quarter 1995, and consistent with industry trends."

A spokesman was not immediately available to elaborate on the net credit loss rate. In the third quarter, the corporation as a whole recorded pre-tax earnings of $101.8 million, $56.1 million of that attributed to Providian Bancorp.
